blog.title: When to chase the cherry blossoms in Japan
blog.body: The blossom front moves north at roughly 25 km a day. Tokyo usually peaks in the last days of March, Kyoto in the first week of April, and Hokkaido in early May. Build a loose itinerary and keep two days of slack: a single rain shower can end peak bloom overnight. Book hotels in Kyoto at least six months out; weekends sell out first.

blog.title: Your first cruise: five things nobody tells you
blog.body: Pick a deck mid-ship for the least motion. Book specialty dining on day one, not day three. Shore excursions through the ship cost more than independent ones, but they guarantee the ship will wait. Pack a lanyard, a power strip without surge protection (many lines ban surge strips) and a light layer for the air-conditioned theatre.

blog.title: Reading the Great Migration like a guide
blog.body: The herds reach the Mara River between July and September, but the exact crossings depend on rain in the Serengeti. Guides watch for restless clusters at the bank and the behaviour of the zebra, who tend to lead. Patience matters more than a long lens: sit with one crossing point for a full morning.

blog.title: Iceland in February: what to pack and what to skip
blog.body: Bring waterproof outer layers, merino base layers and ice cleats. Skip the heavy snow boots: insulated waterproof hikers with cleats work better on wet black sand. Keep your camera battery in an inside pocket and charge your phone every night; the cold drains both faster than you expect.
